_why: The colours every Perceptionism Lab dashboard must agree about, named once.
Three apps deploy separately and cannot read each other at runtime, so each
keeps its own stylesheet. That duplication is the risk this file covers. On
2026-08-19 the client dashboard was measured and rebuilt -- a fourth text
step so the palest shade could stop carrying words, a desaturated good/bad
pair, one flat card surface. Eight days later the agency screen was still
running the version that rebuild replaced, because nobody remembered to copy
it across, and its navigation, filters, column headers and every explanatory
sentence sat at 4.1:1 -- under the readable floor -- on the screen that
So the roles are named here and asserted from both sides. A ROLE, not a
variable name: the two codebases name the same colour differently (--surface
against --card, --green against --color-positive) and forcing one naming on
the other would be a rewrite rather than a check. What must not differ is the
Anything genuinely allowed to differ is NOT in here. A file that lists things
nobody intends to keep equal is one whose failures get waved through.

page_background.note: The ground everything sits on. Contrast ratios are measured against this.

card_surface.note: One flat fill for every raised surface. Was a white gradient over the page, which needed the page behind it to be doing something -- it is flat dark, so the gradient only greyed the card.

input_surface.note: Inputs, selects, popovers and menus. A step lighter than a card on purpose: it reads as something you can type into rather than something you read.

text_secondary.note: Sentences a person reads in full.

text_tertiary.note: Labels and captions. 7.8:1 -- the floor for anything carrying words.

text_decoration.note: SEPARATORS, UNITS, AND A DASH STANDING IN FOR A NUMBER. 4.1:1, under the 4.5:1 readable floor, so it may never carry words. It was the most-used text colour on both dashboards until it was measured.

gold_100.note: The ramp is complete on purpose: Tailwind emits nothing for a shade that does not exist, so a missing one fails silently and the element inherits the page's foreground.

gold_500.note: The brand. Carries no verdict -- it marks what is ours, never whether something is good.

gold_dim.note: Gold at 20%, for a border or a wash.

positive.note: Deliberately desaturated. A saturated green beside this gold reads as a traffic light and drags the whole page towards dashboard-template.

negative.note: The pair to positive, and the ONLY red. #ef4444 is the saturated one both apps removed; where it survives, it survived by being in a variable nobody re-read.

amber.note: Reserved for one thing: how far the page can be trusted. Never a third verdict colour.

_banished_why: Colours the palette REMOVED, which must not reappear as a literal anywhere.
The token check passed while fifteen elements on the Sales Command Center
still rendered #ef4444: it had been taken out of the variables and left in
four component files as a typed hex, plus two login pages in the other repo.
A check that reads only the tokens reports a screen it has not looked at.

banished.#ef4444: The saturated red. Use `negative` (#f4776b) -- a saturated red beside this gold reads as a traffic light.
banished.#34d399: The saturated green. Use `positive` (#6ee7a8), for the same reason.
banished.#71717a: NOT banished as a value -- it is `text_decoration` -- but it may never carry words. Nothing automatic can check that; it is here so the next reader knows.
